claims.text: Local atomic compositional heterogeneities create regions of reduced cohesive energy in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Regions of reduced cohesive energy act as nucleation sites for surface premelting.
Local compositional heterogeneity governs the overall melting behavior of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
The initial nanoparticles are equiatomic and have a homogeneous elemental distribution.
Changes in synthesis or thermal processing can produce measurable compositional segregation while permitting a uniformly mixed control.
The induced segregation may enrich regions in elements having lower bonding energies.
Local chemical composition can affect the energetic stability of interfacial regions.
Surface or interface compositional gradients preferentially concentrate elements with lower melting points or weaker bonds.
Atomic-level compositional inhomogeneities lower local melting energy.
Compositionally inhomogeneous regions begin to premelt before the bulk of the nanoparticle.
The extent and continuity of low-cohesion regions determine the onset and breadth of the melting transition.
More compositionally heterogeneous nanoparticles will begin surface premelting at lower temperatures than a homogeneous control.
More compositionally heterogeneous nanoparticles will exhibit broader melting transitions than a homogeneous control.
DSC and in situ TEM heating can detect the predicted differences in melting onset, transition breadth, and surface premelting.
The hypothesis applies over approximately 0.8 to 1.2 times the nominal melting temperature.
The hypothesis applies to nanoparticles approximately 5–50 nm in size.
The hypothesis applies when constituent elements have notable differences in bonding strength and melting point.
The magnitude of melting-point depression and transition broadening depends on elemental combinations and the degree of heterogeneity.
A lack of statistically significant melting-onset depression or transition broadening in the heterogeneous sample relative to the homogeneous control would falsify the hypothesis.
